primary_claim: Across 39 OLMo-3-7B training checkpoints, harmfulness subcategories do not converge into a single unified direction but occupy a structured, entangled geometric space that forms mostly early in training; in-distribution AUROC for linear harmfulness probes is often misleadingly high (even near initialization) due to superficial lexical and structural cues rather than learned semantic structure; and directions only become stable, transferable, and effective as steering vectors from mid-to-late pretraining onward, with post-training checkpoints steering the Instruct model far more effectively than pretraining-derived directions.

effect.metric: AUROC of general-harmfulness direction under a random-label control (20 repeated label-randomizations)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Confirms and extends Wang et al. (2025, arXiv:2509.03888)'s finding that in-distribution AUROC is not a reliable indicator of a direction's semantic representativeness
Qualifies standard harmfulness-steering practice of treating refusal rate as a harmfulness readout, citing Zhao et al. (2025)'s finding that LLMs encode refusal and harmfulness as separable concepts
stated_future_work: determine what causes the sharp non-monotonic AUROC jumps at specific checkpoints
determine whether the post-training directional shift is primarily a global basis rotation or also alters concept-specific axes
build a curated OOD truthfulness evaluation analogous to the harmfulness one to compare training-stage dynamics
determine why reducing harmfulness (negative steering) has only a limited effect on refusal
determine what changes around ~s1-80k make harmfulness directions substantially more stable and transferable
limitations_stated: refusal and harmfulness aren't the same thing (Zhao et al. 2025 find they're separable concepts), so refusal rate is only a behavioral proxy, not a direct readout of the representation
checkpoint spacing is non-uniform, so differences between adjacent checkpoints may partly reflect spacing choice rather than pure training dynamics
cannot fully rule out that some block boundaries in the checkpoint-similarity analysis (e.g. base-to-SFT) reflect large unmeasured gaps between sampled checkpoints
quote: Harmfulness subcategories do not converge to a single direction, but instead occupy a shared yet structured geometric space.
